original.description: Iqlet is derogatory internet slang for someone seen as unintelligent, built from IQ plus -let. Learn its meaning, origin and how it shows up online.
original.short_definition: Iqlet (also IQlet) is a derogatory internet insult for a person considered very unintelligent or foolish, similar to calling someone an idiot.
original.body_markdown:
## What does iqlet mean

"Iqlet", also written "IQlet", is derogatory internet slang for a person considered very unintelligent or foolish. It works roughly like "idiot" or "moron", according to [Wiktionary](https://en.wiktionary.org/wiki/iqlet). It is a put-down, not a description of anyone's measured intelligence.

In practice, people usually aim it at a specific action or opinion rather than at a person in general. An [Urban Dictionary](https://www.urbandictionary.com/define.php?term=iqlet) entry describes using it to say someone did something a very low IQ person would do. Usage on TikTok stretches the meaning further. One aggregated [TikTok page](https://www.tiktok.com/discover/iqlet-meaning-slang) describes it as a label for someone perceived as having low intelligence or holding a belief others consider incorrect. The same page says it is often used to mock someone's views in online arguments. In many threads it is effectively shorthand for "I disagree with your take."

The available definitions are community-sourced and loose, so read the word in context. Beyond "stupid person", it has no settled meaning.

## Origin

Wiktionary gives the etymology as IQ plus the suffix "-let". The same pattern appears in "brainlet", which [Know Your Meme](https://knowyourmeme.com/memes/brainlet) describes as a 4chan pejorative implying someone has a small brain. Know Your Meme traces the earliest archived use of "brainlet" to the /sci/ board in December 2015. [Digital Cultures](https://digitalcultures.net/memes/brainlet/) notes that the "-let" works as a diminutive suffix.

Iqlet follows the same structure with "IQ" as the base. No source documents when or where iqlet itself was coined, so treat the brainlet link as a structural parallel rather than proven descent. The Urban Dictionary entry compares the two directly. It suggests brainlet is more of a picture, while iqlet describes an action.

## How it relates to looksmaxxing

Iqlet is not a looks term. It belongs to the broader meme and imageboard slang that many online communities share, including the "-let" family of insults that frame a trait as smallness. You may run into it in forum arguments, usually aimed at someone's question or opinion rather than their appearance.

In our editorial view, a thread that turns into labels like iqlet has usually stopped being useful. The insult tells you nothing about your face or your intelligence. If you want feedback grounded in visible features instead, [Aura's AI Face Analysis](https://app.aura-looksmaxxing.com/tools/ai-face-rating?source=%2Fglossary%2Fiqlet) provides a facial profile, a feature breakdown and personal styling suggestions. Its scores are subjective photo-based estimates, not objective attractiveness measurements.
examples: He called me an iqlet for asking a basic skincare question, which said more about him than about me.
Calling every newcomer an iqlet just makes the forum harder to learn from.
In that argument, "iqlet" was really shorthand for "I disagree with you."
